cards.hearing: You may hear that the Fed just raised interest rates again, the first hike like this in a while, and that more could follow.
cards.why: The Fed sets short-term interest rates, and those rates ripple into things like credit cards, car loans, and mortgages, so when they move, borrowing can cost a little more.
cards.but: But the Fed has raised and lowered rates many times over the years, and long-term plans are built to ride through all of it.
cards.story: Picture a thermostat in a big house. Sometimes it gets nudged up, sometimes down, and the house still runs fine because it was built for all kinds of weather. Your plan is built the same way, for warmer rates and cooler ones.
say: We built your plan expecting rate moves like this one.
One rate decision does not rewrite a long-term plan.

cards.hearing: You may hear that stocks had a solid day on Friday, closing the week on a firmer note.
cards.why: A green day feels good, but no single day tells us much about where your retirement will be years from now.
cards.but: But the real win is staying in the game long enough to let good days and bad days average out over time.
cards.story: Picture a farmer checking the weather every single morning and deciding whether to keep the whole farm based on one sunny day. The smart farmer plants, waters, and lets the season play out.
say: A good Friday is nice, but it is one day out of thousands in your plan.
We stay focused on the season, not the forecast.

cards.hearing: You may hear a lot of noise about the midterm elections, big campaign spending, and even talk of court fights over voting rules.
cards.why: Election season can feel loud because it touches taxes, regulations, and who controls Congress, and that uncertainty can make the news feel urgent.
cards.but: But stocks have moved through election after election, red, blue, and everything in between, and your plan was built to do the same.
cards.story: Think of election season like a long stretch of changing weather forecasts. You might see rain predicted, then sun, then rain again, but you still plan your week around the season, not the five-day guess. The plan holds even when the forecast keeps flipping.
say: Elections come and go, and your plan is built for all of them.
We don't trade on predictions. We stick with the plan we made together.
